screen.title: Why Cats Purr
screen.directions: Read an Academic Passage — lower module
text: Cats purr when they are happy, but that is not the only reason. A cat may also purr when it is hurt, hungry or scared. Mother cats purr to their kittens, and kittens purr back to show that they are fine.

Some scientists think purring helps cats calm down. Others believe the low sound may even help bones and muscles heal faster. Cats make the sound by moving muscles in their throat very quickly as they breathe in and out.
Even after many studies, scientists still do not fully agree on why cats purr.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How scientists study the bones of cats
How mother cats take care of their kittens
Why cats are happier than other pets
The different reasons a cat might make a certain sound

questions.stem: The word "heal" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
options: get better
grow longer
move faster
feel colder

questions.stem: Why do kittens purr back to their mothers?
options: To ask their mothers for more food and milk
To show their mothers that they are fine
To show that they are scared
To help their bones grow

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a cat that is purring?
options: It has just finished eating.
It is always hungry when it purrs.
It is not always feeling good.
It wants to play with people.

why.en: Inference: cats in pain or afraid also purr → purring does not always mean the cat feels good.
why.tr: Çıkarım: acıyan/korkan kedi de mırlar → her zaman iyi hissettiği anlamına gelmez.
why.es: Inferencia: los gatos que sienten dolor o miedo también ronronean → ronronear no siempre significa que el gato esté bien.

questions.stem: How do cats produce the sound?
options: By closing their mouth very tightly
By pushing air out through the nose very quickly
By tapping their paws on the ground
By quickly moving muscles in the throat
